{'index': 0, 'translation': 'As the John Ternus era unfolds, Apple is undergoing more leadership changes. A new Bloomberg report today indicates that Apple has appointed a new head of mergers and acquisitions, as well as a new vice president for the App Store.'}

{'index': 1, 'translation': "9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Sony's top-of-the-line BRAVIA TVs are seeing massive price cuts, ranging from entry-level models to flagship offerings — shop now and enjoy the deals!"}

{'index': 2, 'translation': 'According to the report, Apple has appointed Steve Smith as its new head of mergers and acquisitions. Smith takes over from Adrian Perica, who joined Apple in 2009 and led the mergers and acquisitions and corporate development teams for over a decade. Bloomberg describes Smith as Perica\'s "longtime deputy" and reports that he will report to CFO Kevan Parekh.'}

{'index': 3, 'translation': 'Meanwhile, Perica will take on a "more prominent role" within Apple\'s Services division. He has been responsible for iCloud, Fitness+, and Apple News since 2023, and will now report directly to services chief Eddy Cue.'}

{'index': 4, 'translation': 'In fact, both Perica and Apple Music chief Oliver Schusser are seen as potential successors to Cue.'}

{'index': 5, 'translation': 'Additionally, Bloomberg also noted today that Apple is promoting Carson Oliver to vice president of the App Store, reporting to Cue. The App Store was previously overseen by Apple Fellow Phil Schiller, until his retirement in August.'}
